items.title: Consequences of finite global dimension for tor dimension and tor amplitude
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma records three consequences of a ring having finite global dimension d: every module has tor dimension at most d, a complex whose cohomology is concentrated in an interval has tor amplitude shifted by d, and finite tor dimension is equivalent to having bounded cohomology. The proof notes that the hypothesis means every module admits a finite projective resolution of length at most d, which gives the first statement directly, and then derives the second from the cohomology criterion for tor amplitude and the first statement, the third being a rewriting of the second.
